articles.title: Why Israel's claims cannot be accepted at face value
articles.summary:
Why Israel's claims cannot be accepted at face value

Submitted by Faisal Hanif on Fri, 10/16/2026 - 14:00
Any statement from Netanyahu, who has a long and troubling history of twisting the media to serve his agenda, deserves rigorous scrutiny
People walk through the entrance to the BBC’s offices in London on 11 November 2025 (AFP)
Off

Every journalism student learns the same lesson: if your mother says she loves you, check it out. A claim is not a fact until it has been tested, and the more power and self-interest behind it, the more rigorously it should be tested.

A BBC Verify investigation has put that principle to a stark test. It identified 254 incidents in which the Israeli military said it was investigating allegations that its forces had killed or injured people in Gaza, Lebanon, the occupied West Bank and Israel, but for which no public outcome could be found.

Of the 300 cases examined, only 28 had outcomes published on the Israeli army's website. The BBC says it repeatedly approached the military about the cases but received information on only two, both still under review.

The findings do not establish that every allegation is true or that every investigation should lead to prosecution. They raise a basic question: what value does "Israel says" have if the public is never told the eventual outcome?

Yet in Britain, applying that rule to Israel risks arousing the ire of those whose entire purpose is predicated on promoting or defending the Zionist state narrative.

MP Ayoub Khan, who has been derided as a “Gaza independent” by the British media for his advocacy against Israel’s genocide in Gaza, was recently denounced by a slew of media and politicians for questioning the speed of Israel’s inquiry into the Flydubai incident that resulted in an emergency landing late last month. 

Yet Khan’s refusal to simply accept Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s word deserves to be taken seriously, mainly because the ire was not reserved for him alone. 

The BBC was attacked for adhering to proper editorial standards by putting the word “hero”, used by Netanyahu, in quotation marks in its coverage of the Indian pilot who was stabbed on the Israel-bound flight.

Sam Kiley, an experienced foreign editor for the Independent, was condemned for asking who stood to gain from the incident, daring to suggest that it served Netanyahu as he seeks re-election. 

Netanyahu had warned of potential attacks ahead of the 27 October vote. After the Flydubai incident, both he and Defence Minister Israel Katz said it proved them right. 

Asking who benefits from an event, and from how it is framed, is one of the oldest questions in political analysis. The charge against these critics is that doubt itself reveals prejudice. In reality, it is the other way around: credulity is the failure.

Pushing a narrative

This is not paranoia. It is the historical record.

In 1954, Israeli military intelligence recruited Egyptian Jews to bomb British- and American-owned sites in Egypt, intending to blame the attacks on the Muslim Brotherhood and communists. Israel long denied involvement and only honoured the surviving agents in 2005.

Netanyahu's 'eighth front': Israel's billion-dollar war on the truth is failing
Read More »

After the October 2023 Hamas attack, a spokesperson for Netanyahu said babies had been found decapitated. The claim reached British front pages, and former US President Joe Biden said he saw photos of the beheadings. The White House later had to walk back his claim, which has since been debunked. 

The pattern is always the same: a confident assertion that rapidly spreads, becoming part of the folklore that seeks to paint Israel as a perpetual victim, before later being shown to be false.

“Netanyahu says” is a record of what a politician wants the public to believe. “An Israeli official told us” is the same claim with all accountability stripped out. Neither proves anything. That something was said can be reported, but whether it is true must be shown. Relaying it without that additional work is transcription, not journalism.

Remarkably, British news outlets have repeatedly given Israel’s prime minister a megaphone to deride Britain, however absurd his claims. After the UK recognised the state of Palestine, Netanyahu moved to rile an already Islamophobic nation with a jibe about the “Islamic Republic of Britain” - a premise that collapses on the facts: Britain is a constitutional monarchy in which Muslims make up around 6 percent of the population. 

After Britain imposed a settlement trade ban, Netanyahu told the Daily Mail that it had become a “rogue state” under Prime Minister Andy Burnham and accused the Labour government of “appeasing an Islamist-leftist alliance”. He has also reiterated the assertion that Israel helped Britain to thwart an Iranian-backed attack on RAF Fairford, another incident with serious question marks attached.

Where the reporting starts

All of this raises another question: why does an individual facing an International Criminal Court arrest warrant for alleged war crimes and crimes against humanity command so much space in British media? Why is the quote the headline and the evidence an afterthought?

Perhaps Israel’s targeting of major British journalists - including Piers Morgan, Mehdi Hasan and Owen Jones, alongside American commentator Hasan Piker - offers one explanation. All have been, in various ways, critics of Israel’s killing of Palestinian civilians and journalists. Given its well-documented killings of journalists, Israel does not appear to tolerate dissent. 

According to the Committee to Protect Journalists, Israel has killed more than 200 journalists and media workers since October 2023. The committee notes that Israel has repeatedly accused journalists of militant involvement “without producing credible evidence”.

It is reasonable for anyone to ask whether Israel is the ally its supporters describe. Journalists cannot help the public to answer that question if they simply relay its statements verbatim

The cost of deference is self-censorship, and the evidence of it is stark. The Centre for Media Monitoring found the BBC gave a rationale for Israeli military actions in 75 percent of articles on attacks or suffering in Gaza, compared with 17 percent for Russian actions in Ukraine. It challenged Israel’s justifications in 41 percent of cases, compared with 55 percent for Russia. 

The centre also found that the BBC reported the deaths of just 6 percent of 176 Palestinian journalists killed by the Israeli army, compared with 62 percent of journalists in Ukraine. 

With independent journalists barred from Gaza, the world relies on Palestinian reporters and statements from Israeli officials to understand what is happening. If qualifying an Israeli claim brings complaints and political attacks, the response is often silence.

It is reasonable for anyone to ask whether Israel is the ally its supporters describe. Journalists cannot help the public answer that question if they simply relay its statements verbatim. Their job is to scrutinise and challenge. “Israel says” is where the reporting starts, not where it ends.

While brave voices in the trade continue to speak out after three years of genocide in Gaza, “Israel says” remains the routinely used phrase. This is exactly when questions should sharpen.

When trusted media outlets decline to ask the obvious questions, rumours fill the gap. Every question a mainstream newsroom fails to investigate is a question handed to someone who will answer it badly.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz transits remain 70% below pre-conflict levels: UK maritime agency
articles.summary: Shipping traffic through the Strait of Hormuz remained about 70% below pre-conflict levels as attacks on commercial vessels continued, a UK maritime agency said Friday. In its weekly overview, the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency (UKMTO) reported 125 outbound and 129 inbound transits over the past seven days. The figures marked a decline from 129 outbound and 146 inbound transits recorded the previous week, according to the agency. UKMTO reported 12 attacks on vessels during the week, including 10 in the Strait of Hormuz, one in the Gulf and one in the Gulf of Oman. archive.security_status_cs: V regionu nadále přetrvává vysoké napětí kvůli aktivitám v okolí Hormuzského průlivu a rostoucím obavám z širší konfrontace s Íránem, přestože USA signalizují omezení některých vojenských možností. Izrael se připravuje na blížící se parlamentní volby, zatímco v Gaze a Sýrii přetrvávají vážné humanitární a bezpečnostní výzvy včetně napětí na syrské hranici.
archive.security_status_en: High tension persists in the region due to incidents around the Strait of Hormuz and mounting concerns over a broader confrontation with Iran, even as the US signals limitations on certain military actions. Israel is preparing for upcoming parliamentary elections, while grave humanitarian and security challenges persist in Gaza and Syria, including border tensions.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující diplomatický tlak kolem íránského jaderného programu a zvýšenou volatilitu na trzích s ropou v důsledku situace v Zálivu. Politická kampaň v Izraeli bude nadále dominovat místnímu zpravodajství a ovlivňovat tržní náladu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued diplomatic pressure regarding Iran's nuclear program and heightened volatility in oil markets due to the Gulf situation are expected. Israel's political campaign will continue to dominate local news and influence market sentiment.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá kvůli přetrvávajícím střetům na Západním břehu, eskalaci kolem dodávek do Gazy a diplomatickým jednáním ohledně Sýrie a Libanonu. Írán navzdory sankcím nadále částečně exportuje energie, zatímco napětí v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu navyšuje rizika pro námořní dopravu a dodávky ropy.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region remains highly tense due to ongoing clashes in the West Bank, escalation regarding aid deliveries to Gaza, and diplomatic maneuvers concerning Syria and Lebanon. Despite sanctions, Iran continues partial energy exports, while rising tensions near the Strait of Hormuz increase risks to maritime traffic and oil supplies.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující diplomatické manévry ohledně Sýrie a Libanonu, přičemž napětí v Hormuzském průlivu bude nadále udržovat zvýšenou nervozitu na trzích s ropou.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued diplomatic maneuvers regarding Syria and Lebanon are expected, while tensions in the Strait of Hormuz will continue to maintain heightened nervousness in oil markets.

archive.security_status_cs: Situace v Gaze a na Západním břehu zůstává vysoce nestabilní kvůli pokračujícím střetům, přičemž mezinárodní tlak na Izrael roste kvůli humanitární krizi a osadnickému násilí. Současně eskaluje napětí v oblasti Hormuzského průlivu, kde dochází k útokům na plavidla a roste americký a spojenecký vojenský dohled.
archive.security_status_en: The situation in Gaza and the West Bank remains highly volatile amid ongoing clashes, with international pressure mounting on Israel over the humanitarian crisis and settler violence. Simultaneously, tensions in the Strait of Hormuz are escalating with vessel attacks and heightened US and allied military posture.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další diplomatické třenice ohledně Západního břehu a Gazy, přičemž narušení námořní dopravy v Hormuzském průlivu bude nadále udržovat vysokou volatilitu cen ropy.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further diplomatic friction regarding the West Bank and Gaza is expected, while disruptions to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz will continue to sustain high volatility in oil prices.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu se výrazně vyhrotila kvůli přímým útokům na ropné tankery v Hormuzském průlivu, kde údajná exploze námořní miny poškodila supertanker. Zároveň eskaluje napětí na Západním břehu Jordánu po útocích osadníků na palestinské civilisty a zahraniční novináře, což vyvolalo ostrou mezinárodní kritiku. Írán a jeho regionální proxy sítě nadále udržují vysokou míru konfrontace, zatímco diplomatický tlak ze strany USA a Číny roste.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region has escalated significantly due to direct attacks on oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, where a reported naval mine blast damaged a supertanker. Concurrently, tensions are mounting in the West Bank following settler attacks on Palestinian civilians and foreign journalists, drawing sharp international criticism. Iran and its regional proxy networks continue to maintain a high level of confrontation, while diplomatic pressure from the US and China intensifies.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat eskalaci napětí kolem Hormuzského průlivu, která udrží ceny ropy na zvýšených úrovních. Západní březek a diplomatická rovina budou čelit dalším tlakům kvůli střetům a otázkám lidských práv.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, an escalation of tensions around the Strait of Hormuz is expected, keeping oil prices elevated. The West Bank and diplomatic spheres will face continued pressure due to clashes and human rights concerns.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá kvůli přetrvávajícím střetům na Západním břehu, operacím v jižní Sýrii a nestabilitě v Libanonu a Iráku. Mezinárodní tlak roste v souvislosti s humanitární situací v Gaze a zhoršující se dopravní situací v oblasti Perského zálivu.
archive.security_status_en: The security situation in the region remains highly tense due to persistent clashes in the West Bank, operations in southern Syria, and instability in Lebanon and Iraq. International pressure is mounting regarding the humanitarian situation in Gaza and the deteriorating shipping conditions in the Persian Gulf.

archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, persistent tensions in the Gulf and ongoing diplomatic pressures on Israel regarding West Bank developments are expected.
